notes:
Pages opened: Corduene, Adiabene, Peace of Nisibis (299), Jovian (emperor), Roman-Parthian Wars (five: the budget). The Corduene page is thin: no infobox, no capital, no rulers with dates, several sentences without years and some garbled ones, so most of this dossier is bridging; the Cliopatria shapes are kept (ok) because nothing opened contradicts them.

Cliopatria shapes: area 13.9-14.3 k km2, Bohtan and the Tigris left bank; the page names Bohtan, Cizre and the left bank of the Tigris and gives no area, so there is no infobox comparison. The 114-126 gap (Trajan) and the years 260-298 have no shape; the new keyframes gordyene_114 and gordyene_260 carry shapes through at confidence 1 (the page is silent).

End date: Cliopatria ends in 259; the pages put Corduene under Diocletian ('conquered again ... in the 3rd century') and in the 299 cession, and the Jovian page keeps it Roman until 363, so the dossier ends in 299 with Rome as successor. That 260-298 interval is the researcher's reading: who ruled Gordyene then (a Sasanian vassal or satrapy) is not on any page opened. After 299: 363, Jovian's treaty returns Corduene to Persia (Jovian page); a later Roman re-annexation in 578 is on the Corduene page; the Arabs took the area in 640.

Disagreements: the Corduene page dates a peace to 296, the Peace of Nisibis page to 299; the five satrapies differ between the two lists on the Peace page; the Corduene page has 'He took control over parts of Armenia and Mesopotamia' about 115, a sentence that does not parse. Adiabene held Gordyene as a dependency from the late 1st century BC to about 116 (Adiabene page; recorded in the kingdom-of-adiabene dossier as a vassal_start/vassal_end). The Parthian dossier (me-06-a) has Gordyene as a Parthian vassal from about 95 BC, retaken by Tigranes 88-85 BC, and contest 67-65 BC; none of that is on the Corduene page.

Gazetteer: no 'Gordyene' or 'Corduene' region exists; the shape is used instead. Wanted: a region 'Gordyene (Corduene)' for the Bohtan country, Sirnak-Siirt-Batman on the left bank of the Tigris. No capital is named on the page, so identity.capitals is empty (the Tigris fort Bezabde, 'Pinaca', appears in the 360 account and is not a capital).
